politics_vmc_bracket.question: Alabama Senate Election Margin of Victory
politics_vmc_bracket.description:
This market will settle to Yes if the Republican Party nominee's margin of victory in the 2026 Alabama Senate election is between 0% and 5%. Outcome sourced from relevant state election authorities.

The margin of victory is calculated as the absolute difference in vote share percentages between the candidate that receives the most valid votes in the specified election and the candidate that receives the second-most valid votes in the specified election. A candidate's vote share percentage will be calculated by dividing the total number of valid votes received by the candidate by the total number of valid votes cast in the election.

If the specified candidate does not receive the most valid votes in the specified election, this market will settle to No. If the margin falls exactly on the boundary between two ranges, the Contract will settle in favor of the range for which that value is the inclusive lower boundary. If multiple candidates tie for the most votes in the specified election, Yes contract holders of the lowest bracket contract for each tied candidate receive $1.00 divided by the number of tied candidates, rounded down to the nearest tick, per contract.
politics_vmc_bracket.title: Republican 0-5%

politics_cmovc_margin.question: Closest Senate Race?
politics_cmovc_margin.description:
This market will settle to Yes if the 2026 Kansas US Senate election has the smallest margin of victory of any US Senate election held in 2026. Outcome sourced from relevant state election authorities.

The margin of victory for each election is the absolute difference in vote share percentages between the candidate that receives the most votes in the election and the candidate that receives the second-most votes in the election. A candidate's vote share percentage will be calculated by dividing the total number of valid votes received by the candidate by the total number of valid votes cast in the election.

Where an election is tabulated by ranked-choice or instant-runoff voting, the margin of victory is measured in the final round of tabulation that determines the winner. Where an election includes a potential runoff or second round, the margin of victory is measured in the final round that determines the winner.

This market considers all US Senate elections, including special elections, scheduled as of October 31, 2026 to be held in November 2026, including the results of runoff elections held after November 2026. If two or more of those elections have identical smallest margins of victory, Yes contract holders for each tied election receive $1.00 divided by the number of tied elections, rounded down to the nearest tick, per contract.
politics_cmovc_margin.title: Kansas

An IPO is confirmed when i) the SEC declares the specified companys Form S-1 or equivalent registration statement effective, or an equivalent filing with an alternative recognized national securities regulator is approved and made public ii) the IPO is priced (e.g., through a final pricing press release or submission of SEC Form 424B4) or iii) a public securities exchange assigns the specified company a ticker symbol and announces that the company has been approved for initial listing pursuant to an IPO. climate.question: Where Will 2026 Rank Among the Hottest Years on Record?
climate.description:
This market will settle to Yes if 2026 ranks fifth hottest or lower on the Global Land-Ocean Temperature Index. Outcome sourced from NASA GISS.

The relevant figure will be found in the table titled "Land-Ocean Temperature Index (C)" under the column "No_Smoothing" in the row "2026" at https://data.giss.nasa.gov/gistemp/graphs/graph_data/Global_Mean_Estimates_based_on_Land_and_Ocean_Data/graph.txt. 

Years are ranked in descending order by the Global Land-Ocean Temperature Index, starting with the hottest as number 1, the second hottest as number 2, and so on, across all years for which the index has data.

If 2026 is tied with another year in the ranking, the tied rank governs. For example, if 2026 is tied for 2nd, it is ranked 2nd (not 3rd).

Settlement will be based on the data as first published by NASA GISS. Subsequent revisions will not be considered.
climate.title: 5th Or Lower
